id: title:Gilbert09:explain an exhausted rate limit instead of generic transient copy

review.posthog_relevance: Adds customer-facing guidance and regression tests for HTTP 429 rate-limit errors in warehouse ingestion, supporting reliability and user clarity for warehouse sync failures.
review.reason: Adds a new method returning a customer-facing message for HTTP 429 errors and a parametrized test to verify this behavior and guidance. This represents a substantive, bounded improvement in warehouse ingestion reliability and user communication.
review.uncertainty: The actual production impact and adoption are not demonstrated; this is a code implementation and test addition without evidence of resolved incidents or measured benefit.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new method get_retry_exhausted_errors returning a dict with an HTTP 429 error and a customer-facing message advising to reduce sync frequency.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies customer guidance for rate-limit exhaustion, distinguishing it from permission errors; this could help PostHog users understand why a warehouse sync failed and what action to take.

observations.behavior: Adds an import for error_message_matches and a parametrized test checking that 429 errors are not classified as non-retryable and that the guidance message contains the expected advice.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds regression test coverage for the new rate-limit behavior and its customer-facing guidance, supporting reliability of warehouse ingestion workflows.
